examples: The two theories have only a tenuous connection to each other.
His hold on first place was tenuous after the latest scandal.
cloze: The defense relied on a {{tenuous}} argument that few jurors found convincing.
mnemonic: TENUous = thin, like TENUe thread (tenuis = thin).

definition: only slightly warm; unenthusiastic
examples: The tepid coffee had been sitting for an hour, and it was neither hot nor cold when he finally tasted it.
Audiences gave the play a tepid response, offering only faint, halfhearted applause before filing quietly out of the theater.
cloze: The candidate's {{tepid}} speech failed to excite the crowd.
mnemonic: TEPID: TEP, half-hot.

definition: using few words, sometimes in a curt way
examples: His terse reply, a single curt word, ended the discussion before anyone could ask a follow-up question.
The general issued a terse statement and left without taking questions.
cloze: The memo was {{terse}}, giving orders without any explanation.
mnemonic: TERSE sounds like TERSE = tear off extra words.

definition: as a result of that; by that means
examples: The company cut its energy use, thereby saving millions of dollars.
Trees absorb carbon dioxide, thereby slowing the pace of climate change.
cloze: The government lowered interest rates, {{thereby}} encouraging families to borrow and spend more.
mnemonic: THERE + BY: by that, because of that.

definition: to grow or develop successfully
examples: Cacti thrive in dry conditions where other plants die.
Trade flourished and the port city thrived in the sixteenth century.
cloze: Coral reefs {{thrive}} in warm, clear, shallow water with plenty of sunlight.
mnemonic: THRIVE: THRIVing = alive and well.

definition: to prevent someone from accomplishing something; to frustrate
examples: Heavy snow thwarted our attempt to reach the summit, forcing the whole expedition to turn back before noon.
Police acted quickly to thwart the planned robbery, arresting the suspects before they could reach the bank doors.
cloze: Rising costs could {{thwart}} the company's plan for expansion.
mnemonic: THWART: 'Th'-WART the plan like a wart blocks.

definition: showing nervousness or fear; timid
examples: The timorous child hid behind her mother's legs when the dog barked.
A timorous speaker, he mumbled through the presentation and avoided eye contact.
cloze: The {{timorous}} candidate refused to debate for fear of being embarrassed.
mnemonic: TIMORous: TIMid + horror.

definition: a long, angry speech of criticism or accusation
examples: The coach launched into a furious tirade against the referees.
Her tirade about the late train lasted a full five minutes.
cloze: The manager's {{tirade}} left the whole office stunned and silent.
mnemonic: TIRADE: you get TIRED of listening to it.

definition: a state of sluggishness or inactivity; lethargy
examples: In the summer heat the town sank into a torpor that lasted until dusk.
After the long meal, a pleasant torpor settled over the diners.
cloze: The bear lay in a winter {{torpor}} for months, barely breathing.
mnemonic: TORPor: TORPedoed by sleep, can't move.

definition: to promote or praise enthusiastically, often to attract attention
examples: Advertisements tout the new phone as the fastest ever built.
Politicians often tout their achievements loudly during campaigns while conveniently ignoring their failures and broken promises.
cloze: Companies {{tout}} their products loudly in the hope of attracting buyers.
mnemonic: TOUT rhymes with SHOUT: shout out praise to sell something.

definition: a small sign showing that something existed
examples: Scientists found traces of ancient pollen in the sediment.
The storm left no trace of the village.
cloze: The fossil contains a faint {{trace}} of the creature's last meal.
mnemonic: TRACE: follow the TRACKs.

definition: easy to control or influence; manageable
examples: The tractable horse calmly followed its handler without complaint, easily guided wherever the rider wished to go.
With patient teaching, even the most stubborn child became tractable.
cloze: A {{tractable}} workforce accepted the new rules without protest.
mnemonic: TRACTor pulls things along: easily led.

definition: a compromise in which one gains one thing by losing another
examples: Faster travel often involves a tradeoff between speed and safety.
Economists describe a tradeoff between lower prices and higher quality.
cloze: There is a clear {{tradeoff}} between protecting forests and expanding farmland.
mnemonic: TRADE one thing OFF for another.

definition: to change completely in form or nature
examples: A caterpillar transforms into a butterfly inside its chrysalis.
The railroad transformed the western economy by linking distant markets.
cloze: Heat and pressure can {{transform}} limestone into marble over millions of years.
mnemonic: TRANS-FORM: cross over to a new FORM.

definition: to go beyond the limits of a law or moral rule; to violate
examples: Those who transgress the safety code by breaking its rules will face heavy fines and possible suspension.
He did not mean to transgress, but he ignored the unwritten rules of the club.
cloze: Citizens who {{transgress}} the law are subject to punishment.
mnemonic: TRANS-GRESS: step ACROSS (trans) a line.

definition: lasting only a short time; temporary
examples: The island's population is transient, rising in summer and falling in winter.
Her fame proved transient, fading within a year as the public quickly moved on to the next celebrity.
cloze: A {{transient}} workforce of seasonal pickers moves in each autumn.
mnemonic: TRANSient: you TRANSit through and leave.

definition: to send or pass something from one place to another
examples: Mosquitoes transmit diseases such as malaria between people.
Nerve cells transmit signals to the brain in milliseconds.
cloze: Parents {{transmit}} traditions to their children through stories and rituals.
mnemonic: TRANS (across) + MIT (send): send across.

definition: sharp, forceful, and effective in expression
examples: The critic wrote a trenchant analysis that exposed the film's flaws.
Her trenchant wit cut through the pompous speeches of the evening.
cloze: He offered a {{trenchant}} critique of the plan that left its authors speechless.
mnemonic: TRENCHant: a TRENCH is cut sharply into the ground.

definition: a general direction in which something is changing
examples: Researchers noticed a trend toward earlier springs in the region.
Economists track consumer trends to predict future demand.
cloze: Over the past century there has been a steady {{trend}} toward urban living.
mnemonic: TREND: what is TRENDing now.

definition: to cause something to start or happen
examples: Heavy rain can trigger landslides on steep slopes.
The assassination triggered a chain of events that led to war.
cloze: Changes in day length {{trigger}} many animals to begin migrating.
mnemonic: TRIGGER of a gun starts the action.

definition: overused and lacking originality; commonplace
examples: The movie's trite plot, full of worn-out clichés, offered no surprises to anyone who had seen similar films.
The speaker closed with a trite phrase about following your dreams.
cloze: His {{trite}} advice, such as 'be yourself', was the sort heard a thousand times.
mnemonic: TRITE sounds like TIRED: a tired phrase.

definition: eager to argue or fight; aggressively defiant
examples: The truculent customer shouted at the staff and demanded to see the manager.
Negotiations stalled because of the delegate's truculent attitude, as he glared and argued over every minor point.
cloze: The {{truculent}} teenager answered every question with a snarl.
mnemonic: TRUCulent: a TRUCK driver in a road rage.

definition: a loud, confused noise or commotion
examples: The tumult in the stadium, a roar of confused shouting, drowned out the announcer's voice completely.
In the tumult of the evacuation, with loud panic and confusion everywhere, many families were separated from one another.
cloze: A {{tumult}} of voices rose from the crowd.
mnemonic: TUMULT: tumble in noise.

definition: loud, chaotic, and disorderly
examples: The tumultuous crowd surged toward the gates, shouting and pushing in a chaotic wave that police could not control.
It was a tumultuous period in the nation's history, marked by riots, sudden upheavals, and constant political turmoil.
cloze: The star was greeted with {{tumultuous}} applause.
mnemonic: TUMULT: a mob in turmoil.

definition: characterized by conflict, disorder, or violent movement
examples: The plane shook in the turbulent air over the mountains.
The country went through a turbulent period of strikes and protests.
cloze: The {{turbulent}} sea tossed the small boat like a toy.
mnemonic: TURBULENT: TURBine whirling air.

definition: a beginner or novice
examples: The tyro made several mistakes during his first week on the job.
Even a tyro can learn the basics of the program in an afternoon.
cloze: As a {{tyro}} in chess, she lost the match within a few moves.
mnemonic: TYRO sounds like 'tire-oh': a newbie whose tires are not yet worn.

definition: present or found everywhere
examples: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life, appearing in nearly every pocket, office, and classroom around the world.
The coffee chain's green logo is ubiquitous in the city.
cloze: Plastic is now so {{ubiquitous}} that traces are found even in remote oceans.
mnemonic: YOU-BIQUITOUS: YOU, everywhere you go!

definition: final or most important; the last in a series
examples: The ultimate goal of the project is to protect endangered habitats.
The ultimate cause of the empire's fall remains a matter of debate.
cloze: After years of negotiation, the {{ultimate}} decision rested with the council.
mnemonic: ULTIMATE = last: ULTIMATEly.

definition: to experience or be subjected to something
examples: Metamorphic rocks undergo changes under intense heat and pressure.
Patients must undergo several tests before the treatment begins.
cloze: Cities often {{undergo}} major changes when a new industry arrives.
mnemonic: UNDER + GO: go through something.

definition: forming the hidden basis of something
examples: Researchers sought the underlying causes of the economic crisis.
The underlying rock of the island is volcanic basalt.
cloze: The {{underlying}} principle of the theory is that energy cannot be created or destroyed.
mnemonic: UNDER + LYING: lying beneath the surface.

definition: to weaken gradually or secretly
examples: Constant rumors began to undermine the team's confidence in its leader.
Corruption can undermine public trust in the courts, slowly weakening faith in the fairness of the entire legal system.
cloze: Frequent interruptions {{undermine}} the speaker's authority.
mnemonic: UNDER + MINE: dig a mine under a wall.

definition: to emphasize or highlight
examples: The recent flood underscores the need for better drainage, since it shows how badly the city is protected.
Her remarkable success underscores the value of hard work, highlighting how steady effort can lead to great achievement.
cloze: The results {{underscore}} the importance of early diagnosis.
mnemonic: Draw a line UNDER the SCORE of the point.

definition: leaving no doubt; clear and unambiguous
examples: The judge gave an unequivocal ruling in favor of the tenants.
The evidence was unequivocal: the fire had been set deliberately.
cloze: The senator made an {{unequivocal}} denial of the charges.
mnemonic: UN-EQUI-VOCAL: not two (equi) voices, a single clear voice.

definition: remaining the same in all cases
examples: The workers were paid a uniform rate regardless of their experience.
The temperature in the lab must be uniform to ensure the results are valid.
cloze: The coastline is not {{uniform}}; some stretches are rocky and others are sandy.
mnemonic: UNI (one) + FORM: one form.

definition: never having happened before
examples: The region suffered an unprecedented drought last summer.
The telescope provided unprecedented images of distant galaxies.
cloze: The company's {{unprecedented}} growth surprised even its founders.
mnemonic: UN + PRECEDENT: nothing before it.

definition: not able to be defended or justified
examples: His position became untenable after the evidence emerged, since there was no longer any reasonable way to defend it.
The court ruled that the argument was untenable, because it could not be supported or defended by any facts.
cloze: The manager's stance was {{untenable}} in light of the data.
mnemonic: UN-TENable: cannot be held (tenere = hold).

definition: not justified or authorized
examples: The harsh criticism was unwarranted and unfair, since the team had done nothing to deserve such blame.
He was angered by the unwarranted intrusion into his private life, which had no justification whatsoever.
cloze: Her {{unwarranted}} suspicion damaged an innocent person's reputation.
mnemonic: UN-WARRANT-ed: has no warrant.

definition: to seize power or a position by force or without right
examples: The general tried to usurp the throne while the king was abroad.
Critics said the committee had usurped powers belonging to parliament.
cloze: Rebels plotted to {{usurp}} the authority of the legitimate ruler.
mnemonic: U-SURP: 'you SURPrise me, you took my seat!'

definition: to make practical use of something
examples: Some birds utilize tools, such as sticks, to extract insects from bark.
Ancient farmers utilized river floods to fertilize their fields.
cloze: The company plans to {{utilize}} solar power to cut its electricity bills.
mnemonic: UTILize = UTILITY: put it to use.

definition: to waver between different opinions or actions
examples: He tended to vacillate between accepting the job and staying put.
The senator vacillated for weeks, swinging between support and opposition, before finally announcing her vote on the bill.
cloze: Do not {{vacillate}}; make a decision and stick with it.
mnemonic: VACILLATE: VASE on a sill wobbles back and forth.

definition: lacking thought or intelligence; empty
examples: The actor gave a vacuous grin and said nothing of substance.
Critics dismissed the film as a vacuous spectacle with no real story.
cloze: His {{vacuous}} speech was filled with slogans but no real ideas.
mnemonic: VACUOUS: VACUUM, nothing inside.

definition: not clear or precise
examples: The map gave only a vague idea of the island's location.
The instructions were so vague that students interpreted them differently.
cloze: A {{vague}} memory of the lecture was all she could recall during the exam.
mnemonic: VAGUE sounds like WAVE: blurry and uncertain.

definition: reasonable and logical; legally acceptable
examples: Critics raised valid concerns about the sample size of the study.
A valid passport is required to travel abroad.
cloze: For the results to be {{valid}}, the experiment must be repeatable by other scientists.
mnemonic: VALID: VALue holds up.

definition: lacking liveliness, flavor, or interest
examples: The vapid conversation drifted from weather to nothing at all.
Critics found the sitcom vapid and its characters flat, noting that nothing in it was interesting or original.
cloze: The {{vapid}} novel offered no fresh insight or memorable character.
mnemonic: VAPID: VAPor, no substance.

definition: a factor that can change in an experiment
examples: Scientists change only one variable at a time to see its effect.
Rainfall is a key variable in determining how well crops grow.
cloze: Temperature was the only {{variable}} that differed between the two groups of plants.
mnemonic: VARIABLE: it can VARY.

definition: exhibiting different colors or varied forms
examples: The variegated leaves of the plant were splashed with white and green.
His career was a variegated mix of teaching, writing, and business.
cloze: The garden's {{variegated}} blooms made a patchwork of color.
mnemonic: VARIEgated: VARIEty of colors.

definition: to differ or change from one case to another
examples: Temperatures in the desert vary widely between day and night.
Diet and habitat vary among the different species of finches.
cloze: Prices of grain {{vary}} depending on weather conditions and demand.
mnemonic: VARY: VARIETY comes from it.

definition: extremely large in size or amount
examples: Vast deserts cover much of North Africa.
The library contains a vast collection of historical maps.
cloze: A {{vast}} network of rivers drains the Amazon basin.
mnemonic: VAST sounds like VAST-ocean: huge.

definition: showing strong feeling; forceful
examples: He issued a vehement denial of the rumor, speaking with such intense force that no one doubted his anger.
She was a vehement opponent of the plan, arguing against it with passionate and uncompromising force at every meeting.
cloze: The senator's {{vehement}} objection stopped the proposal.
mnemonic: VEHEMENT: a VEHicle moving at fierce speed.

definition: open to bribery; corrupt
examples: The venal judge ruled in favor of whoever paid the most.
Reformers accused the police force of being venal and unaccountable.
cloze: A {{venal}} official, he would approve any permit for a price.
mnemonic: VENAL = VENDable: can be bought.

definition: to regard with deep respect and reverence
examples: Many cultures venerate their elders for their wisdom, treating them with deep respect and listening carefully to their advice.
The villagers venerate the old temple as a sacred place.
cloze: Students {{venerate}} their teacher, hanging on every word he says.
mnemonic: VENERate: VENus is revered.

definition: truthfulness; accuracy
examples: No one in the courtroom doubted the veracity of the witness's account, because every detail matched the physical evidence.
Editors checked the veracity of every quotation before publication to make sure that each statement was accurate and true.
cloze: The lawyer challenged the {{veracity}} of the claim made in the report.
mnemonic: VERACity: VERY true.

definition: using more words than needed
examples: The verbose report could easily have been cut in half.
His verbose explanation left the audience more confused than before.
cloze: A {{verbose}} writer buries a simple idea under paragraphs of words.
mnemonic: VERBose: VERBs piled upon verbs.

definition: to check that something is true or accurate
examples: Journalists must verify facts before publishing a story.
Scientists verified the results by repeating the experiment three times.
cloze: Carbon dating helped {{verify}} that the manuscript was written in the twelfth century.
mnemonic: VERI (true) + FY: make sure it is true.

definition: a trace or remnant of something that no longer exists
examples: The wall is the last vestige of the ancient fortress.
Not a vestige of the old village remained after the flood.
cloze: A small {{vestige}} of the old custom survives in the town's festival.
mnemonic: VESTIGE: a footstep left, like a 'vest' left behind.

definition: to annoy or frustrate; to trouble
examples: The constant noise from the street began to vex the tired residents.
It vexed her that no one had told her about the change.
cloze: Nothing could {{vex}} him more than waiting in a long line.
mnemonic: VEX sounds like HEX: a hex annoys.

definition: capable of working or succeeding; practicable
examples: The engineers said the plan was viable if funding could be secured.
Without enough water, the seedlings were no longer viable and could not grow into healthy plants no matter what.
cloze: Is a four-day work week economically {{viable}} for small firms?
mnemonic: VIABLE: it has a VIA (way) to live.

definition: experienced through another person rather than firsthand
examples: She took vicarious pleasure in her daughter's success, feeling joy as though she herself had won the prize.
Reading travel stories gave him a vicarious thrill of adventure.
cloze: Fans enjoyed a {{vicarious}} triumph through their team's victory.
mnemonic: VICARious: a VICAR lives holy life for you.

definition: keeping careful watch for possible danger
examples: Guards remained vigilant throughout the long night, watching closely for any sign of danger near the walls.
A vigilant nurse noticed the change in the patient's breathing.
cloze: Parents must stay {{vigilant}} when children play near the water.
mnemonic: VIGIL: a night watch.

definition: to speak about in an abusively critical way
examples: The tabloids tried to vilify the minister with false accusations.
She was vilified by her opponents, who twisted her words and spread cruel falsehoods to ruin her reputation.
cloze: Rivals sought to {{vilify}} the candidate in a smear campaign.
mnemonic: VILE-ify: make someone seem vile.

definition: to clear of blame or suspicion; to prove right
examples: New evidence vindicated the man who had been imprisoned for years.
The eventual success of the project vindicated her bold decision, proving that the doubters had been wrong all along.
cloze: The inquiry was expected to {{vindicate}} the accused engineer.
mnemonic: VINDICATE: Vin-dicate, 'win' your case.

definition: having a strong desire for revenge
examples: The vindictive manager fired anyone who disagreed with him, determined to punish every person who had ever crossed him.
She refused to be vindictive after the betrayal and instead forgave her rival, wishing to take no revenge at all.
cloze: A {{vindictive}} rival spread rumors out of a desire for revenge.
mnemonic: VINDICTIVE: VINDICtive wants to get you back.

definition: extremely severe or harmful; bitterly hostile
examples: A virulent strain of flu spread rapidly through the town.
The newspaper published a virulent attack on the mayor, filled with bitter hostility and savage personal insults.
cloze: The {{virulent}} disease killed thousands before a vaccine arrived.
mnemonic: VIRULENT: VIRUS-lent.

definition: absolutely necessary for life or success
examples: Water is vital for all forms of life on Earth.
Wetlands play a vital role in filtering pollutants from rivers.
cloze: It is {{vital}} that researchers record every step of the procedure accurately.
mnemonic: VITAL = VITamin for life.

definition: filled with bitter, harsh criticism
examples: The editorial was vitriolic in its condemnation of the mayor.
A vitriolic email from the customer left the staff shaken.
cloze: The senator's {{vitriolic}} attack on his rival shocked the audience.
mnemonic: VITRIOL = sulfuric acid; words that burn.

definition: lively, animated, and spirited
examples: The vivacious hostess charmed all the guests with her bright laughter, quick wit, and endless lively energy.
Her vivacious, bubbly personality brightened every meeting and made even the dullest agenda feel lively and fun.
cloze: The {{vivacious}} young singer filled the stage with energy.
mnemonic: VIVacious: VIVa, full of life!

definition: expressing opinions loudly and forcefully
examples: Vociferous protesters filled the square, shouting loudly and demanding change from the government without pausing for breath.
He was a vociferous critic of the new policy, objecting loudly and forcefully at every public meeting.
cloze: The crowd grew {{vociferous}} when the referee ignored the foul.
mnemonic: VOCIFERous: VOICE + FERocious.

definition: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably; explosive
examples: The volatile situation could erupt into violence at any moment.
Oil prices are volatile, swinging sharply from week to week.
cloze: Her {{volatile}} temper made even small disagreements explode.
mnemonic: VOLATILE: evaporates and flies off like a volley.

definition: an amount of space or quantity; a book in a series
examples: The volume of water flowing through the river doubles after the spring thaw.
The library holds over a million volumes, including rare medieval texts.
cloze: A large {{volume}} of data was collected from satellites orbiting the planet.
mnemonic: VOLUME: how much fills the space.

definition: having an insatiable appetite for food or activity
examples: The voracious lion devoured the entire carcass in minutes, tearing at the meat with its enormous appetite.
She was a voracious reader, finishing three books a week.
cloze: A {{voracious}} appetite for novels kept him in the library daily.
mnemonic: VORACIOUS: devour + Voracious = 'VORE' (eat).

definition: easily harmed, attacked, or damaged
examples: Young sea turtles are vulnerable to predators when they cross the beach.
Coastal villages are especially vulnerable to rising seas and storms.
cloze: Without natural defenses, the island's native birds were {{vulnerable}} to invasive rats.
mnemonic: VULNERABLE: a VULNERABLE spot gets WOUNDed.

definition: to decrease gradually in strength or size
examples: Public interest in the scandal began to wane after a few weeks.
The moon waxes and then wanes in a regular cycle.
cloze: As evening came, the daylight started to {{wane}} over the hills.
mnemonic: WANE is WAN (pale) as it fades.

definition: deliberate and unprovoked; cruel or reckless
examples: The wanton destruction of the old forest outraged the town.
Police condemned the wanton vandalism of the cemetery, a senseless and cruel act committed with no reason at all.
cloze: The {{wanton}} cruelty of the attack shocked even hardened veterans.
mnemonic: WANTON: wants to hurt for no reason, 'want-on' to destroy.

definition: cautious about possible dangers or problems
examples: Wary of strangers, the stray cat approached the visitor very slowly, ready to bolt at the slightest movement.
Investors are wary of risky stocks after recent heavy losses, preferring to proceed with great caution this year.
cloze: She was {{wary}} of the offer, suspecting a hidden catch.
mnemonic: WARY: BE-WARE.

definition: to be indecisive; to shift unsteadily
examples: His resolve began to waver when he saw the cost.
The candle flame wavered unsteadily in the cold draft, flickering back and forth as if it might go out.
cloze: Despite the pressure, the council did not {{waver}} in its decision.
mnemonic: WAVER: WAVE back and forth.

definition: by which; through which
examples: The treaty created a system whereby neighboring countries shared river water.
The company introduced a policy whereby employees could work from home.
cloze: Scientists developed a process {{whereby}} seawater is turned into drinking water.
mnemonic: WHERE + BY: by where; by which means.

definition: playfully quaint or fanciful; unpredictable
examples: The whimsical garden was filled with gnomes and tiny bridges.
Her whimsical, playful sense of humor surprised everyone, since no one could ever predict what odd joke she would make.
cloze: The artist's {{whimsical}} drawings delighted children with talking animals.
mnemonic: WHIM: a sudden fancy.

definition: found or happening over a large area
examples: Illiteracy was widespread in the region before public schools were built.
Drought caused widespread crop failure across the plains.
cloze: The practice of terrace farming became {{widespread}} throughout the mountainous regions.
mnemonic: WIDE + SPREAD: spread wide.

definition: skilled at gaining an advantage by cunning
examples: The wily fox cleverly outsmarted the hounds, using cunning tricks and a hidden path to escape the hunt.
A wily negotiator, he made concessions that cost him nothing.
cloze: The {{wily}} merchant talked the tourists into a price twice the usual.
mnemonic: WILY: WILe, trick like a wily coyote.

definition: attractive and charming in an innocent way
examples: The winsome child won over the entire audience with her smile.
Her winsome manner made her a favorite of her colleagues.
cloze: A {{winsome}} grin and polite words made him popular with teachers.
mnemonic: WINsome: you WIN people over.

definition: having a feeling of vague, melancholy longing
examples: He cast a wistful glance at his old school, longing sadly for the happy years he had spent there.
She spoke in a wistful tone about her childhood home.
cloze: The old sailor gave a {{wistful}} sigh as he watched the ships depart.
mnemonic: WISTful: WISH full of sadness.

definition: to remove or take back something
examples: Troops were withdrawn from the region after the treaty was signed.
Students may withdraw from a course before the end of the second week.
cloze: The pharmaceutical company decided to {{withdraw}} the drug after reports of side effects.
mnemonic: WITH + DRAW: draw back with you.

definition: to shrivel or fade from lack of water, vigor, or support
examples: Without rain, the crops began to wither in the fields.
Her hopes withered slowly after the third rejection letter arrived, until she almost stopped believing she would succeed.
cloze: Flowers {{wither}} quickly when kept in the hot sun.
mnemonic: WITHER: WITHout water, you shrivel.

definition: to resist or endure without giving way
examples: The ancient temple has withstood earthquakes for over two thousand years.
Some bacteria can withstand extreme heat near volcanic vents.
cloze: The tower was designed to {{withstand}} winds of over two hundred kilometers per hour.
mnemonic: WITH + STAND: stand against it.

definition: important or valuable enough to justify time or effort
examples: Educators believe field trips are worthwhile experiences for students.
The long journey proved worthwhile when the team discovered the ancient tomb.
cloze: Scholars considered the costly expedition {{worthwhile}} because of the knowledge it produced.
mnemonic: WORTH + WHILE: worth your while.

definition: to produce or provide a result or crop
examples: Improved seeds yield much larger harvests than traditional varieties.
The excavation yielded hundreds of pottery fragments and several tools.
cloze: Careful analysis of tree rings can {{yield}} a record of past climate.
mnemonic: YIELD: crops YIELD; cars YIELD. Both give way.

definition: amusingly unconventional and idiosyncratic
examples: The zany comedian jumped around the stage in a clown costume.
Their zany antics, absurd and wildly unconventional, made the show a hit with audiences of every age.
cloze: The film features a {{zany}} cast of eccentrics.
mnemonic: ZANY: a ZANY ZANY clown.

definition: great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause
examples: The volunteers worked with great zeal to clean the beach, tireless and eager from the first morning to the last.
He pursued his studies with remarkable zeal, rising at dawn each day because of his burning enthusiasm for learning.
cloze: Her {{zeal}} for reform inspired the entire movement.
mnemonic: ZEAL: ZEst + ideAL.

definition: a person fanatically committed to a cause
examples: The political zealot, fanatical about his cause, refused to compromise on any detail no matter how small it was.
Moderates feared the zealots would drag the party to extremes.
cloze: The religious {{zealot}} ignored every argument against his beliefs.
mnemonic: ZEALot: a ZEAL-ot has too much zeal.

definition: the highest point or period of success
examples: The empire reached its zenith in the second century, enjoying the greatest power and wealth in its long history.
At the zenith of her career, she won three awards in a year.
cloze: The sun reached its {{zenith}} at noon, directly overhead.
mnemonic: ZENITH: Z is the last letter; the top.

definition: an area with a particular feature or purpose
examples: Tropical rainforests are found in the equatorial climate zone.
The city created a pedestrian zone in the old town center.
cloze: Fish are abundant in the shallow {{zone}} of the lake where sunlight reaches the bottom.
mnemonic: ZONE: a Zoned-off piece of land.
